notes: The first lower bound in this development proved in Lean, and with the rank-2 decomposition of StrangeM2Pointwise it settles chi(|S>^2) = 2 with both directions machine-checked. Lower bounds are universally quantified, which is why the rest of the Lean development proves only upper bounds; at r = 1 the quantifier is over a single state and one structural fact closes it with no enumeration. The support of a stabilizer state is an affine subspace of F_3^n, so it is closed under a - b + c. |S>^2 is supported on the four points of {1,2}^2, and taking a = c = (1,1) with b = (2,2) lands on (0,0), where the amplitude vanishes. The affine-support property enters as a hypothesis rather than being derived, exactly as the Pointwise files carry stabilizer-ness in the shape of their definitions; anything satisfying it is covered, so the theorem is strictly more general than the stabilizer case.
